engagement.scope_ref: Static analysis of owned teaching fixture only

summary.executive_en: Static review of the training sample found a critical insecure posture: hardcoded cloud/database secrets, SQL injection, and an unauthenticated command-execution endpoint. Two high issues enable cross-user invoice access and secret exfiltration via a debug route. The application must not be deployed; remediate critical and high items before any real use.
summary.executive_de: Die statische Prüfung des Trainings-Samples zeigt eine kritische Sicherheitslage: fest kodierte Cloud-/Datenbank-Geheimnisse, SQL-Injection und ein nicht authentifizierter Befehlausführungs-Endpunkt. Zwei hohe Findings ermöglichen fremden Rechnungszugriff und Geheimnisabfluss über eine Debug-Route. Die Anwendung darf nicht betrieben werden; kritische und hohe Punkte vor jeder realen Nutzung beheben.

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in source
findings.description: Production-like database password and cloud secret are embedded in application source. Anyone with repository, backup, or image access obtains live credentials suitable for data theft and cloud abuse.

evidence.summary: Hardcoded postgres URL with password and AWS secret access key constant

remediation.guidance: Remove secrets from source; load from a secret manager or runtime env; rotate all exposed credentials immediately; add secret scanning (gitleaks/trufflehog class) to CI and block merges on hits.
remediation.retest_notes: Confirm secrets absent from tree and git history scan; verify rotation timestamps.

findings.business_impact: Full database and cloud account compromise; regulatory exposure if personal data is reachable.

findings.title: Broken object-level authorization on invoices (BOLA)
findings.description: Invoice records are loaded by invoice_id only. The user_id path parameter is not used for authorization, so any caller who can hit the endpoint may read other users' invoices.

evidence.summary: Query filters only on invoice id; no owner/tenant check against authenticated user

remediation.guidance: Enforce invoice.owner_id == auth.user_id (or tenant scope) before return; deny with 404/403 on mismatch; add automated cross-user access tests.
remediation.retest_notes: Attempt cross-user invoice fetch; expect denial.

findings.business_impact: Confidential financial/customer invoice data leakage across accounts.

findings.title: SQL injection in product search
findings.description: User-controlled query parameter q is interpolated into SQL via an f-string. An attacker can alter the query to read, modify, or destroy data.

evidence.summary: f-string builds SQL with unsanitized q
evidence.snippet: db.execute(f"SELECT * FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{q}%'")

remediation.guidance: Use parameterized queries only (e.g. LIKE ? with bound value). Prefer an ORM. Add SAST rule for string-built SQL.
remediation.retest_notes: Injection payloads in q must not alter query structure.

findings.business_impact: Database compromise; potential full application takeover.

findings.title: OS command injection with missing authentication
findings.description: The admin_run endpoint executes caller-supplied cmd via shell=True with no authentication or authorization. This is direct remote code execution if the service is reachable.

evidence.summary: subprocess.check_output(cmd, shell=True) on request JSON without auth

remediation.guidance: Remove the endpoint or replace with a fixed allowlist of operations; never use shell=True on user input; require strong admin authentication and authorization; place behind network controls.
remediation.retest_notes: Endpoint absent or rejects unauthenticated calls; no shell interpolation.

findings.business_impact: Complete host compromise; lateral movement into internal networks.

findings.title: Debug config endpoint exposes secrets and environment
findings.description: A debug endpoint returns the database URL, AWS key material, and the full process environment to any caller.

evidence.summary: JSON response includes database_url, aws_key, and dict(os.environ)

remediation.guidance: Delete the endpoint outside local development; never return secrets; gate any diagnostics behind admin auth and explicit non-production checks.

findings.business_impact: Credential and configuration theft enabling further compromise.

findings.title: Flask debug server bound to all interfaces
findings.description: The application entrypoint runs Flask with debug=True and host 0.0.0.0, which is unsafe if exposed beyond localhost (debugger and verbose errors).

remediation.guidance: Use a production WSGI server (gunicorn/uvicorn); debug=False; bind localhost only for local development.
remediation.retest_notes: Production process is not Flask dev server; debug disabled.

findings.business_impact: Increased attack surface and information leakage if network-exposed.
